content.text:
I read the structure as a symmetric Boc-protected glutamic acid core carrying two identical arms, one on each carbonyl.

**Core.** The central unit is Boc-NH-CH(C(=O)NH-CH2CH2-NH-…)-CH2CH2-C(=O)NH-CH2CH2-NH-…. Each carbonyl is amidated with ethylenediamine.

**Each arm.** The free ethylenediamine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O)CH2CH2CH2-O-aryl, a 4-oxybutanoyl linker. The aryl group is a 3,5-dimethyl-4-sulfonylphenyl ring, so the sulfonyl carbon sits between the two methyl groups. The sulfonyl is S(=O)(=O)NH-CH(COOH)-CH2-NH-C(=O)-indazole, a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit.

**Indazole and tail.** The indazole is attached through its 5-carboxamide, and N1 carries the chain CH2CH2CH2-NH-(2-imidazolyl).

**Stereochemistry.** The top arm has a wedge on the bond from the alpha carbon to COOH. I assigned this as the L (S) configuration, giving N[C@@H](CN...)C(=O)O in that arm. The bottom arm is drawn without a clear wedge, so I left it unspecified. The glutamic acid centre is plain, so it is also unspecified.

**SMILES for one arm**, written from the sulfonamide nitrogen:
N[C@@H](CNC(=O)c1ccc2c(cnn2CCCNc2ncc[nH]2)c1)C(=O)O, with the sulfonyl on N.

For the top arm I wrote the alpha carbon as [C@@H] with neighbours in the order N, CH2, COOH. The wedge goes to COOH, and the other neighbours are NH (down), CH2 (left) and H. Viewed from the top, the S/L configuration reads CH2 → NH → COOH. I did not verify the @/@@ choice rigorously, so the chirality tag is a best estimate.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NC(CCC(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(cnn3CCCNc3ncc[nH]3)c2)C(=O)O)c(C)c1)C(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(S(=O)(=O)NC(CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(cnn3CCCNc3ncc[nH]3)c2)C(=O)O)c(C)c1
